items.text: Process tree is correct: cscript.exe → cmdkey.exe, i.exe, cmdkey.exe, with the cmd.exe parent marked as not in evidence
Explained the cmdkey trick: a password stored under Microsoft_Windows_Shell_ZipFolder lets Windows extract a password-protected ZIP silently
Identified i.exe as a renamed cmd.exe using OriginalFileName / Description, and tied that to the alert name
Recognized the elastic-endpoint.exe popup as the security agent's reaction, not attacker activity
Noticed lync.zip's CreationUtcTime (12:05) is hours before it was written, without claiming to know why
Noticed the EventRecordID gaps and concluded the export is partial
Noticed record order ≠ time order (the popup has a later record ID but an earlier time) and sorted by time
Listed at least three things the logs can't tell you (e.g. how testme.js arrived, what i.exe did, who started cmd.exe)
IOC list notes that i.exe's hash is a legitimate cmd.exe hash, useful for hunting renamed copies but not as a 'bad hash'
